title.zh: 卷362 列傳一百四十九 方积 朱尔汉 杨頀 廖寅 陈昌齐 朱尔赓额 查崇华
title.en: Volume 362 Biographies 149: Fang Ji, Zhu Erhan, Yang Hu, Liao Yin, Chen Changqi, Zhu Ergenge, Cha Chonghua
title.raw: 卷362 列傳一百四十九 方积 朱尔汉 杨頀 廖寅 陈昌齐 朱尔赓额 查崇华

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十九

translations.literal: Biographies 149
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 149

sentences.zh: 方積硃爾漢楊頀廖寅陳昌齊硃爾賡額查崇華方積，字有堂，安徽定遠人。

translations.literal: Fang Ji, Zhu Erhan, Yang Hu, Liao Yin, Chen Changqi, Zhu Ergenge, and Cha Chonghua — Fang Ji, courtesy name Youtang, was a native of Dingyuan, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats Fang Ji, Zhu Erhan, Yang Hu, Liao Yin, Chen Changqi, Zhu Ergenge, and Cha Chonghua. Fang Ji, styled Youtang, came from Dingyuan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 拔貢生。

translations.literal: A selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the tribute-student selection examination.

sentences.zh: 以州判發四川，補閬中知縣，署梁山。

translations.literal: Dispatched to Sichuan as a subprefectural judge, he was appointed magistrate of Langzhong and served as acting magistrate of Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Sichuan as a subprefectural judge, he received the Langzhong magistracy and acted as magistrate of Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 達州東鄉賊起，梁山當其衝，賊犯縣境，營白兔山守兵潰。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Dongxiang, Dazhou; Liangshan lay in their path. When bandits invaded the county borders, the garrison at White Rabbit Mountain collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rose in Dongxiang, Dazhou, and Liangshan stood directly in their path. When they crossed into the county, the garrison at White Rabbit Mountain broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 積以一百人據小山為疑兵，賊不敢進。

translations.literal: Ji took one hundred men to hold a small hill as a decoy force, and the bandits dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: With a hundred men posted on a small hill as a feint, Fang Ji kept the rebels from pressing forward.

sentences.zh: 築砦二百餘所，令人自為守。

translations.literal: He built more than two hundred stockades and had the people defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified more than two hundred stockades and organized the people to garrison their own defenses.

sentences.zh: 他縣流民依集者三十餘萬人，賊至無所掠食，屢出奇兵擊走之。

translations.literal: More than three hundred thousand refugees from other counties gathered under his protection; when bandits came they had nothing to plunder for food, and he repeatedly sent surprise troops to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Some three hundred thousand refugees from neighboring counties rallied to him; the rebels found nothing left to loot, and he repeatedly routed them with surprise sorties.

sentences.zh: 堅壁清野之法，蓋自梁山始。

translations.literal: The method of fortifying walls and clearing the countryside began, it seems, with Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy of scorched earth and fortified strongpoints appears to have begun at Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 既而萬縣寶靈寺賊起，越境剿平之，又助大兵殲伍文相於石壩山，卻林亮功於望牛埡，斃亮功弟廷相，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon after, rebels rose at Baoling Temple in Wan County; he crossed the border to suppress and pacify them. He also assisted the main army in annihilating Wu Wenxiang at Shiba Mountain, repelled Lin Liangong at Wangniuya, killed Lin Liangong's younger brother Tingsxiang, and was awarded peacock feather insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels broke out at Baoling Temple in Wan County, he crossed into the district and put them down. He then helped the main force destroy Wu Wenxiang at Shiba Mountain, drove Lin Liangong back at Wangniuya, killed Lin's younger brother Tingsxiang, and received peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 擢寧遠知府，仍留駐梁山，凡四年。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Ningyuan, yet remained stationed at Liangshan for four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Ningyuan, he nevertheless stayed on at Liangshan for four years.

sentences.zh: 至嘉慶六年，諸路賊漸平，調夔州，繼劉清為建昌道。

translations.literal: By Jiaqing 6, rebels on the various routes were gradually pacified; he was transferred to Kuizhou and succeeded Liu Qing as Jianchang intendant.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth year of Jiaqing, rebel bands on the main routes were being subdued; he was moved to Kuizhou and succeeded Liu Qing as intendant of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 涼山生番叛，率師討平之。

translations.literal: The raw tribes of Liangshan rebelled; he led troops to subdue and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the raw tribes of Liangshan rose in revolt, he led a campaign that brought them back under control.

sentences.zh: 未幾，里塘正土司索諾木根登殺副土司，奪其印，副將德寧兵為所困。

translations.literal: Before long, the chief native official Suonuomugendeng of Litang killed the deputy native official, seized his seal, and Deputy General De Ning's troops were trapped by him.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, Suonuomugendeng, chief native official of Litang, murdered his deputy, seized the official seal, and trapped Deputy General De Ning's force.

sentences.zh: 積單騎往，密授舊頭目希拉工布方略，以其眾破之。

translations.literal: Ji went alone on horseback, secretly imparted strategy to the former headman Xilagongbu, and with those forces defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ji rode in alone, secretly briefed the former headman Xilagongbu on his plan, and broke the usurper with Xilagongbu's men.

sentences.zh: 歷川北道、鹽茶道，擢按察使。

translations.literal: He served as intendant of Chuanbei Circuit and the Salt-and-Tea Circuit, and was promoted to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as intendant of Chuanbei and of the Salt-and-Tea Circuit, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 馬邊、峨眉嶺諸夷結梁山生番盜邊，積偕提督丰紳由馬邊三河口鑿山深入，克六拔夷巢，遂出赤夷間道，進攻嶺夷十二地。

translations.literal: The various tribes of Mabian and Emeiling joined with Liangshan raw tribes to raid the border. Ji, together with Regional Commander Feng Shen, advanced from Mabian's Sanhekou by cutting through the mountains deep inland, captured the Liuba Yi stronghold, then emerged by a secret path among the Chi Yi and pressed the attack on twelve Ling Yi territories.
translations.idiomatic: When tribes around Mabian and Emeiling joined Liangshan raw tribes in border raids, Fang Ji and Regional Commander Feng Shen cut inward from Sanhekou at Mabian, took the Liuba Yi stronghold, slipped through a hidden route among the Chi Yi, and struck twelve Ling Yi settlements.

sentences.zh: 浹旬之間，每戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Within ten days, every battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In less than two weeks, he won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 曲曲烏助逆死拒，潛師出其後，殄之。

translations.literal: Ququwu aided the rebels and resisted to the death; Ji sent troops secretly around behind them and exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ququwu backed the rebels and fought to the last; Fang Ji sent a hidden force around their rear and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 積官四川二十餘年，馳驅殆遍，山川風土，了然於胸，用兵輒獨當一面。

translations.literal: Ji served in Sichuan for more than twenty years, riding hard until he had covered nearly the whole province; its mountains, rivers, and local customs were clear in his breast, and whenever troops were deployed he single-handedly held one front alone.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ji spent more than twenty years in Sichuan, riding until he had seen nearly every corner of the province; he knew its terrain and people by heart, and in war he was repeatedly entrusted with an independent command.

sentences.zh: 及任籓司，僚屬多故交，一無瞻徇。

translations.literal: When he served as provincial treasurer, many subordinates were old acquaintances, yet he showed no favoritism whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: As provincial treasurer, he had many old friends among his staff, yet he never showed them partiality.

sentences.zh: 清節自勵，​​尤為時稱。

translations.literal: He spurred himself to integrity, and this was especially praised in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself to strict integrity, for which contemporaries especially praised him.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，祀名宦。

translations.literal: He died in office and was enshrined among distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was entered in the temple of eminent local officials.

sentences.zh: 硃爾漢，字麗江，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Zhu Erhan, courtesy name Lijiang, was a native of Daxing, Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Erhan, styled Lijiang, came from Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 少為戶部吏。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served as a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，官甘肅靖遠典史，母憂去官。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he served as jail warden of Jingyuan, Gansu, and left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he held the post of Jingyuan jail warden in Gansu, then resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋待次，時平涼回酋田五作亂，爾漢與通判吳廷芳、知縣黃家駒守靖遠城，賊來攻。

translations.literal: When mourning ended and he awaited reassignment, the Hui chieftain Tian Wu of Pingliang rose in rebellion. Erhan, together with Subprefect Wu Tingfang and Magistrate Huang Jiaju, defended Jingyuan city when bandits came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended and he was awaiting a new appointment, the Hui chieftain Tian Wu of Pingliang rebelled. Zhu Erhan, Subprefect Wu Tingfang, and Magistrate Huang Jiaju held Jingyuan when the rebels attacked.

sentences.zh: 靖遠回豪哈得城等期夜半為內應，爾漢得其情，令守者悉登城不得下，至哈得成家，陽科其穀餉軍，因拘之；

translations.literal: Jingyuan Hui magnate Hade Cheng and others had arranged a midnight rendezvous as inside collaborators. Erhan learned of it, ordered all defenders to mount the walls and not come down, went to Hade Cheng's home, feigned requisitioning his grain to supply the army, and thereby arrested him.
translations.idiomatic: Hade Cheng, a leading Hui figure in Jingyuan, and others had plotted a midnight uprising from within. Zhu Erhan uncovered the plan, kept every defender on the walls, went to Hade Cheng's house under the pretense of requisitioning grain for the garrison, and seized him.

sentences.zh: 分遣人誘擒城下賊，賊之雜守者在城上已數十人，縣役鐵光保最為劇賊，猝擒之。

translations.literal: He dispatched men separately to lure and capture bandits below the wall; several dozen bandit infiltrators were already on the wall, and county runner Tie Guangbao was the fiercest bandit — he was suddenly seized.
translations.idiomatic: He sent parties to lure and capture rebels below the walls. Dozens of infiltrators were already on the ramparts; Tie Guangbao, a county runner and one of the worst rebels, was taken in a sudden rush.

sentences.zh: 角聲起，扼城上賊無脫者，外賊覺，遂引去。

translations.literal: When the horn sounded, those holding the wall-trapped bandits had no escape; the outer bandits realized what had happened and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At the signal horn, the men on the walls closed on the infiltrators and none escaped; the rebels outside realized the plot had failed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 由是以知兵聞，擢隆德知縣。

translations.literal: Thereby he became known for military skill and was promoted to magistrate of Longde.
translations.idiomatic: This won him a reputation as a capable commander, and he was promoted to magistrate of Longde.

sentences.zh: 徙底店砦降回，擢涇州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: He relocated surrendered Hui from Didian Stockade and was promoted to magistrate of the directly administered prefecture of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After resettling surrendered Hui from Didian Stockade, he was promoted to magistrate of the directly administered prefecture of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 擒教匪劉松，擢鞏昌知府。

translations.literal: He captured sect rebel Liu Song and was promoted to prefect of Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the sect rebel Liu Song and was raised to prefect of Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，教匪起，蔓延三省。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 1, sect rebels rose and spread across three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing, sect rebels rose and the rebellion spread across three provinces.

sentences.zh: 二年，四川賊尤熾，總統宜綿駐達州，檄爾漢參軍事。

translations.literal: In year 2, bandits in Sichuan burned especially fierce; Grand Coordinator Yimian was stationed at Dazhou and summoned Erhan to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the rebellion burned hottest in Sichuan; Grand Coordinator Yimian, stationed at Dazhou, called Zhu Erhan to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 是時王三槐踞方山坪，白岩山者，地險固，賊渠林亮功、樊人傑屯山上，與方山坪為聲援。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Sanhuai held Fangshanping; White Rock Mountain was rugged and fortified, with rebel chiefs Lin Liangong and Fan Renjie encamped on the mountain in mutual support with Fangshanping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sanhuai held Fangshanping, while White Rock Mountain — rugged and easily defended — was held by rebel chiefs Lin Liangong and Fan Renjie in mutual support with Fangshanping.

sentences.zh: 將軍舒亮、提督穆克登布屯山前之韓彭坳，爾漢兵三百、鄉勇三千屯山後之排亞口。

translations.literal: General Shuliang and Regional Commander Mukedengbu encamped at Hanpeng'ao before the mountain; Erhan with three hundred soldiers and three thousand local militia encamped at Paiyakou behind the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: General Shuliang and Regional Commander Mukedengbu took up position at Hanpeng'ao on the mountain's front; Zhu Erhan, with three hundred regular troops and three thousand militia, blocked Paiyakou on the rear.

sentences.zh: 排亞口之上曰金鳳觀，曰草店，曰鴨坪，一日盡攻克之。

translations.literal: Above Paiyakou were Jinfengguan, Caodian, and Yaping — all were captured in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Above Paiyakou lay Jinfengguan, Caodian, and Yaping; he took all three in one day.

sentences.zh: 復進，有木柵當隘，不見賊，惟以犬守。

translations.literal: Advancing further, a wooden palisade blocked the pass; no bandits were seen, only dogs standing guard.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing forward, he found a wooden barricade across the defile; no rebels were visible — only dogs on watch.

sentences.zh: 兵躍攀柵，賊自崖旁斫傷之，鳴鑼掣旗，左右賊大至，爾漢慮斷後路，退師。

translations.literal: Troops leaped up to scale the palisade; bandits hacked at them from the cliffside, gongs sounded and flags were raised, and bandits poured in from both flanks. Erhan feared his retreat would be cut off and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: His men scrambled up the palisade; rebels hacked at them from the cliffs, gongs rang and flags went up, and enemy forces swarmed in from both sides. Fearing encirclement, Zhu Erhan pulled back.

sentences.zh: 先是與韓彭坳諸師為期，中道而止，賊得專力山後，故不克。

translations.literal: Earlier he had agreed on a coordinated timing with the forces at Hanpeng'ao, but stopped halfway; the bandits were thus able to concentrate solely on the rear of the mountain, and so victory was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: He had arranged a joint attack with the Hanpeng'ao column, but halted midway; the rebels were therefore free to throw their full strength against the mountain's rear, and the assault failed.

sentences.zh: 既而奉節賊千餘來援，敗之，擒賊渠邱廣福。

translations.literal: Soon after, more than a thousand bandits from Fengjie came to reinforce; he defeated them and captured rebel chief Qiu Guangfu.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a thousand rebels from Fengjie marched to relieve the garrison, he routed them and captured the rebel chief Qiu Guangfu.

sentences.zh: 岩賊久困欲走，傾巢來犯，戰一晝夜不得路，仍退。

translations.literal: The mountain bandits, long besieged and wishing to flee, came out in full force to attack; after fighting day and night without finding a way out, they withdrew again.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain rebels, long trapped and desperate to break out, attacked in full strength; after a day and night of fighting with no escape, they fell back again.

sentences.zh: 爾漢攻之三閱月，博戰被創，乃回鞏昌。

translations.literal: Erhan besieged them for three months, was wounded in fierce fighting, and then returned to Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Erhan pressed the siege for three months, was wounded in heavy fighting, and then returned to Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 三年，運麥十萬石餉軍，行至成縣，賊渠高均德來奪，敗之於格樓壩，擒其黨李德勝。

translations.literal: In year 3, transporting one hundred thousand shi of wheat to supply the army, he reached Cheng County; rebel chief Gao Junde came to seize it; he defeated him at Gelouba and captured his follower Li Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while hauling one hundred thousand shi of wheat to the army, he reached Cheng County; rebel chief Gao Junde tried to seize the grain, but Zhu Erhan defeated him at Gelouba and captured his lieutenant Li Desheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，張漢潮犯秦州，爾漢赴成縣會剿。

translations.literal: In year 4, Zhang Hanchao invaded Qinzhou; Erhan went to Cheng County to join the suppression campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Zhang Hanchao struck at Qinzhou, Zhu Erhan went to Cheng County to join the joint suppression.

sentences.zh: 鞏昌警至，馳還，賊已據城東鴛鴦河，夜掠賊卡而入，城守始固，以功擢鞏秦階道。

translations.literal: An alarm from Gongchang arrived; he galloped back. Bandits had already seized Yuanyang River east of the city; by night he raided through the bandit outposts and entered, and the city's defense was finally secured. For this merit he was promoted to intendant of Gong-Qin-Jie Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Gongchang was threatened, and he raced back. Rebels had already taken Yuanyang River east of the city; he slipped in by night through their outposts, stabilized the defense, and for this service was promoted intendant of the Gong-Qin-Jie Circuit.

sentences.zh: 生番鐵布者，居西傾山中，眾十餘萬，乘教匪猖獗，時出盜內地。

translations.literal: Among the raw tribes was Tiebu, dwelling in the Western Tilting Mountains with a population of more than one hundred thousand; taking advantage of the sect rebels' rampage, they frequently raided the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The raw tribesman Tiebu lived in the Western Qinling Mountains with a following of more than one hundred thousand; while sect rebels ran wild, his people often raided the interior.

sentences.zh: 爾漢以鐵布未叛亂，且地險，一構兵非數年不能平。

translations.literal: Erhan judged that Tiebu had not yet rebelled, and given the perilous terrain, once hostilities were joined it could not be pacified in less than several years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Erhan reasoned that Tiebu had not yet openly rebelled and that, in such rugged country, once war began it would take years to finish.

sentences.zh: 鐵布奉回教，乃召其阿渾諭之，於是來首者踵至。

translations.literal: Tiebu followed Islam; Erhan then summoned their ahun to instruct them, whereupon those who came to surrender arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Tiebu had embraced Islam; Zhu Erhan summoned the Muslim religious leader to counsel the people, and surrenders soon poured in one after another.

sentences.zh: 一日書姓名一紙，曰：此鐵布黨也。

translations.literal: One day he wrote names on a slip of paper, saying: 'These are Tiebu's followers.'
translations.idiomatic: One day he wrote out a list of names and said, "These are Tiebu's partisans."

sentences.zh: 又出一圖，曰：盜巢及要隘盡於此。

translations.literal: He also produced a map, saying: 'The bandits' lairs and strategic passes are all here.'
translations.idiomatic: He then produced a map and said, "Every rebel nest and key pass is marked on this."

sentences.zh: 分遣百餘人捕之，悉就擒，鐵布遂定。

translations.literal: He dispatched over a hundred men to capture them; all were seized, and the Tiebu affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent out more than a hundred men to arrest them; all were captured, and the Tiebu uprising was thus pacified.

sentences.zh: 六年，川、楚、陝賊漸蹙，餘賊多竄甘肅，率兵扼剿，凡數十戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the bandits of Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi were gradually pressed; most of the remaining bandits fled into Gansu. He led troops to block and suppress them, and in several dozen battles was victorious every time.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, as the rebels in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi were increasingly cornered, most of the survivors fled into Gansu. He led troops to intercept and suppress them, winning every one of several dozen engagements.

sentences.zh: 八年，甘肅匪平，上功最，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the bandits in Gansu were pacified; his merit was ranked highest, and he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the rebels in Gansu were suppressed; his achievements were ranked first, and he was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 爾漢有識斷，能得人死力，奴客悉以兵法部之。

translations.literal: Erhan had discernment and decisiveness, could win men's utmost exertion unto death, and organized all his retainers and servants according to military methods.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Erhan was shrewd and resolute, could inspire men to fight to the death for him, and drilled all his retainers and servants according to military tactics.

sentences.zh: 自出仕即在行間，後遂與教匪相終始。

translations.literal: From the time he entered office he was in the ranks; afterward he was involved with the sect rebels from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of his career he served in the field, and he remained engaged with the White Lotus rebels throughout.

sentences.zh: 用兵有法，所用鄉勇侯達海，侍衛李榮華，武舉劉養鵬，千總鄒坤、桂攀桂皆操刺勇健善戰，故所至有功。

translations.literal: He had method in employing troops; the local militiaman Hou Dahai, bodyguard Li Ronghua, military licentiate Liu Yangpeng, and company commanders Zou Kun and Gui Pangui whom he used were all skilled with weapons, brave, sturdy, and good in battle, so wherever he went he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He employed sound military methods, and the men he relied on—the militia leader Hou Dahai, bodyguard Li Ronghua, military licentiate Liu Yangpeng, and company commanders Zou Kun and Gui Pangui—were all expert with arms, brave, hardy, and skilled in combat, so he won success wherever he campaigned.

sentences.zh: 尋調廣東肇羅道，擢廣西按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Zhaoluo Circuit of Guangdong, promoted to Guangxi Surveillance Commissioner, and served as acting Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Zhaoluo Circuit in Guangdong, promoted to Guangxi Surveillance Commissioner, and appointed acting Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 楊頀，字邁功，江西金谿人。

translations.literal: Yang Hu, courtesy name Maigong, was a native of Jinxi in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu, courtesy name Maigong, was a native of Jinxi, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十九年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 總辦秋審，執法平。

translations.literal: In charge of the autumn review, he enforced the law impartially.
translations.idiomatic: As overseer of the autumn judicial review, he applied the law fairly.

sentences.zh: 內監訟其弟妻，頀按律杖贖守夫墓。

translations.literal: A eunuch sued his brother's wife; Hu, according to law, sentenced her to caning with redemption for guarding her husband's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When a palace eunuch sued his brother's wife, Yang Hu, following the law, sentenced her to caning with redemption for failing to guard her husband's tomb.

sentences.zh: 和珅方總刑部，意有所徇，駁詰之，頀面爭。

translations.literal: Heshen was then head of the Ministry of Punishments and wished to show favor; he rejected and cross-examined him, and Hu argued face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen was then in charge of the Ministry of Punishments and wanted to show favor; he overturned the ruling and pressed him, and Yang Hu argued with him directly.

sentences.zh: 和珅叱曰：「司員敢爾！

translations.literal: Heshen shouted: 'A clerk dares thus!'
translations.idiomatic: Heshen rebuked him, saying, "How dare a clerk behave like this!"

sentences.zh: 」頀厲聲曰：「司員主稿，知為刑獄得其平耳！

translations.literal: Hu said in a stern voice: 'The clerk drafts the case and knows only that criminal justice must be balanced!'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu replied sharply, "As the drafting clerk, I know only that justice in criminal cases must be even!"

sentences.zh: 何叱為？

translations.literal: Why shout at me?
translations.idiomatic: "Why rebuke me?"

sentences.zh: 」和珅不能奪。

translations.literal: Heshen could not overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen could not prevail against him.

sentences.zh: 及珅敗，擢員外郎。

translations.literal: When Shen fell, Hu was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: After Heshen's downfall, he was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 仁宗召見，嘉其有守，命解餉四十萬兩赴四川濟軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong summoned him, praised his integrity, and ordered him to convey four hundred thousand taels of silver to Sichuan to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong received him in audience, commended his steadfastness, and ordered him to transport four hundred thousand taels of silver to Sichuan to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 川、陝大吏交章論薦，授陝西延榆綏道。

translations.literal: The high officials of Sichuan and Shaanxi jointly memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed Intendant of the Yan-Yu-Sui Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The senior officials of Sichuan and Shaanxi submitted joint memorials recommending him, and he was appointed Intendant of the Yan-Yu-Sui Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時三省清釐叛產，撫卹難民，事方殷，詔責疆吏慎選公正大員如《音蒦》及劉清者任其事。

translations.literal: At that time the three provinces were sorting out rebel property and providing relief to refugees; the work was pressing, and an edict rebuked frontier officials to choose carefully upright senior officials such as Yang Hu and Liu Qing to take charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the three provinces were clearing rebel estates and providing relief to war victims, and the task was urgent; an edict admonished frontier officials to select carefully upright senior officials such as Yang Hu and Liu Qing to handle it.

sentences.zh: 頀週曆田野，綜覈不苟，民漸復業。

translations.literal: Hu traveled through the fields, examined and verified without laxity, and the people gradually resumed their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu toured the countryside, investigated matters thoroughly and without slackness, and the people gradually returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 巡撫秦承恩檄府縣募民補伍，頀曰：「農工商賈各有其業，若預選送營，曠日失業，與抽丁何殊？

translations.literal: Governor Qin Chengen ordered the prefectures and counties to recruit civilians to fill military ranks; Hu said: 'Farmers, artisans, merchants, and traders each have their own occupations; if they are pre-selected and sent to camp, they lose their livelihoods over many days—how is this different from conscription?'
translations.idiomatic: Governor Qin Chengen ordered the prefectures and counties to recruit civilians to fill military quotas; Yang Hu said, "Farmers, artisans, merchants, and traders each have their own trade; if they are chosen in advance and sent to camp, they lose their livelihoods for days on end—how is that different from conscription?"

sentences.zh: 」議乃寢。

translations.literal: The proposal then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 調甘肅平慶涇固鹽法道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ping-Qing-Jing-Gu Salt Controller's Circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Salt Controller of the Ping-Qing-Jing-Gu Circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年，擢安徽按察使，捕六安州匪劉成巨置諸法。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiaqing, he was promoted to Anhui Surveillance Commissioner; he captured the bandit Liu Chengju of Lu'an Prefecture and brought him to justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Jiaqing reign he was promoted to Anhui Surveillance Commissioner and captured the Lu'an bandit Liu Chengju, bringing him to justice.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷江寧布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred to Jiangning Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Jiangning Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚大水，乘舴艋歷災區訪問疾苦，渡湖幾覆，災黎感之。

translations.literal: When Huai and Yangzhou suffered great floods, he took a small boat through the disaster areas to inquire into people's hardships; crossing a lake he nearly capsized, and the disaster victims were moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai and Yangzhou were struck by major floods, he traveled through the stricken areas in a small boat to inquire into the people's suffering; crossing a lake he nearly overturned, and the flood victims were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 尋以失察山陽知縣王仲漢冒賑，坐褫職。

translations.literal: Soon, for failure to detect that Shanyang Magistrate Wang Zhonghan had embezzled relief funds, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was stripped of his rank for failing to detect that Shanyang Magistrate Wang Zhonghan had misappropriated relief funds.

sentences.zh: 詔頀查賑認真，平日實心辦事，留河工效力。

translations.literal: An edict said Hu's investigation of relief had been conscientious and that in daily affairs he worked sincerely, and he was retained to serve effectively on river works.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Yang Hu had investigated relief conscientiously and had always worked earnestly, and he was retained to serve on river conservancy.

sentences.zh: 復起用，歷淮海道、浙江按察使、江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: Restored to office, he served successively as Huai-Hai Circuit Intendant, Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner, and Jiangsu Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Reinstated, he served in succession as Huai-Hai Circuit Intendant, Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner, and Jiangsu Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was promoted to Zhejiang Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐臨海民毆差釀大獄，降四品京堂；

translations.literal: Before long, because residents of Linhai beat runners and a major case arose, he was demoted to fourth-rank Beijing official.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, after Linhai residents beat government runners and a major case erupted, he was demoted to a fourth-rank capital official.

sentences.zh: 復不俟代去任，降禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Again, without waiting for his successor, he left his post and was demoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Again, without waiting for his replacement, he left his post and was demoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired home.

sentences.zh: 道光五年，重宴鹿鳴，加四品卿銜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang, at the re-gathering banquet for juren, he was granted fourth-rank ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Daoguang reign, at the re-gathering banquet for provincial graduates, he was granted the rank of fourth-rank ministerial official.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 廖寅，字亮工，四川鄰水人。

translations.literal: Liao Yin, courtesy name Lianggong, was a native of Linshui in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yin, courtesy name Lianggong, was a native of Linshui, Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十四年舉人。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 家貧，不能常試禮部，十二年中，僅再至都。

translations.literal: His family was poor and could not regularly go to the Ministry of Rites for the metropolitan examination; in twelve years he went to the capital only twice.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he could not regularly travel to the capital for the metropolitan examination; in twelve years he went to the capital only twice.

sentences.zh: 以大挑知縣官河南，署葉縣。

translations.literal: Through the great selection he was appointed a magistrate in Henan and served as acting magistrate of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Through the great selection he was appointed a magistrate in Henan and served as acting magistrate of Ye County.

sentences.zh: 時教匪方熾，葉當衝，寅撫民不擾。

translations.literal: At the time the sect rebels were raging; Ye was on the front line, and Yin governed the people without disturbing them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the White Lotus rebels were rampant; Ye County lay on the front line, and Liao Yin governed the people without harassing them.

sentences.zh: 民有從逆者，捕其魁乃定。

translations.literal: When the people joined the rebels, he captured the ringleaders and then order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When locals joined the rebellion, he captured the ringleaders, and peace was restored.

sentences.zh: 長子思芳有武略，省父至葉，任以守衛事。

translations.literal: His eldest son Sifang had military talent; he came to Ye to visit his father and was entrusted with guard duties.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Sifang had military ability; he came to Ye to visit his father and was put in charge of security.

sentences.zh: 詔捕教首劉之協，久不獲。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the capture of the sect rebel leader Liu Zhixie, but for a long time he was not caught.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order called for the capture of the rebel leader Liu Zhixie, but he remained at large for a long time.

sentences.zh: 一日，思芳巡歷近郊，見二人縶馬坐樹下語，異之，歸戒門者伺狀。

translations.literal: One day Sifang patrolled the outskirts and saw two men tethering horses and sitting under a tree talking; finding it strange, on returning he warned the gatekeepers to watch for such persons.
translations.idiomatic: One day Sifang patrolled the outskirts and saw two men tether their horses and sit talking under a tree; finding this suspicious, he returned and told the gatekeepers to watch for such men.

sentences.zh: 俄二人入城飲肆中，有識之者，其一即之協。

translations.literal: Before long the two entered the city and drank in a tavern; someone recognized one of them—he was precisely Zhixie.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the two entered the city and drank at a tavern; someone recognized one of them—he was Liu Zhixie himself.

sentences.zh: 寅趣思芳往與雜坐，出不意縛之，鞫得實，​​械至都伏法。

translations.literal: Yin urged Sifang to go and sit with him casually; unexpectedly they bound him, interrogated and obtained the truth, sent him in shackles to the capital, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yin urged Sifang to come and sit casually with Liu Zhixie; they then seized him by surprise, and after interrogation confirmed the facts, sent him in shackles to the capital, where he was executed.

sentences.zh: 特擢江蘇鎮江知府。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to prefect of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to prefect of Zhenjiang, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 濬丹陽九曲河，築徬，以時啟閉，民便之。

translations.literal: He dredged the Jiuchu River in Danyang, built sluice embankments, and opened and closed them at the proper seasons; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Jiuchu River at Danyang, built sluice embankments, and regulated their opening and closing by season, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 擢江西吉南贛道，兼筦關榷，正稅外無多取，吏胥奉法。

translations.literal: Promoted to Jinan-Gan Circuit intendant in Jiangxi, concurrently managing customs levies; beyond the regular tax he took nothing extra, and clerks and runners obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Jinan-Gan Circuit intendant in Jiangxi and concurrently managed customs levies; he collected nothing beyond the regular tax, and clerks and runners obeyed the law.

sentences.zh: 會南昌煽亂，捕首惡置法。

translations.literal: When Nanchang was incited to rebellion, he captured the ringleaders and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion was stirred up in Nanchang, he arrested the ringleaders and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 安遠复亂，單騎往諭，解散黨與，耆民等縛其魁以獻，事遂平。

translations.literal: When Anyuan rebelled again, he went alone on horseback to instruct them, dispersed the gang members, and elders bound their leader and presented him; the matter was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Anyuan rebelled again, he rode there alone to reason with the rebels, dispersed the gang, and local elders bound their leader and handed him over; the disturbance was then pacified.

sentences.zh: 歷署布政使、按察使。

translations.literal: He successively served as acting provincial treasurer and judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as acting provincial treasurer and judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年，遷兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing, he was transferred to Salt Transport Commissioner of Lianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Jiaqing reign, he was appointed Salt Transport Commissioner of Lianghuai.

sentences.zh: 卹灶丁，治私梟，鹽課漸增。

translations.literal: He showed sympathy to salt-furnace workers, dealt with illegal salt smugglers, and salt revenue gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: He looked after the salt-furnace workers, cracked down on illegal salt traders, and salt revenue gradually rose.

sentences.zh: 河北滑縣教匪起，總督百齡檄寅往徐州協守禦。

translations.literal: When sect rebels rose in Huaxian, Hebei, Governor-General Bailing ordered Yin by dispatch to go to Xuzhou to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When White Lotus rebels rose in Huaxian, Hebei, Governor-General Bailing ordered Liao Yin to Xuzhou to help with the defense.

sentences.zh: 會捕逆匪劉第五，誤系同姓名者，坐失察降調，上念其擒劉之協功，許捐復原職。

translations.literal: When capturing the rebel Liu Diwu, he mistakenly detained someone of the same name; for failure of supervision he was demoted and transferred, but the emperor, remembering his merit in capturing Liu Zhixie, permitted him to restore his original rank through donation.
translations.idiomatic: While trying to capture the rebel Liu Diwu, he mistakenly detained a namesake; he was demoted for negligence, but the emperor, recalling his service in capturing Liu Zhixie, allowed him to buy his way back to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 以老病歸，遂卒。

translations.literal: Due to old age and illness he returned home, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired home because of old age and illness, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 思芳少時居鄉治團練，從軍數有功，官至江蘇候補道。

translations.literal: In youth Sifang lived in his village organizing militia; in military service he had repeated achievements, and rose to Jiangsu acting circuit intendant awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Sifang organized local militia in his home district; he won repeated distinctions in military service and rose to acting circuit intendant of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 在葉手擒劉之協，名聞天下。

translations.literal: At Ye he personally captured Liu Zhixie, and his fame spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye County he personally captured Liu Zhixie, and his name became known throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 後以捕劉第五獲罪下獄，尋赦之。

translations.literal: Later, because of the affair of capturing Liu Diwu, he was found guilty and imprisoned; soon he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was imprisoned for the Liu Diwu affair, but was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 陳昌齊，字賓臣，廣東海康人。

translations.literal: Chen Changqi, courtesy name Binchen, was a native of Haikang, Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Changqi, courtesy name Binchen, was a native of Haikang, Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷中允。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed reviser, and was successively promoted to middle attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed reviser, and was successively promoted to middle attendant.

sentences.zh: 大學士和珅欲羅致之，昌齊以非掌院，無晉謁禮，不往。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Heshen wished to recruit him, but Changqi, holding that he was not academy director and had no obligation to pay a formal visit, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Heshen tried to win him over, but Changqi, saying he was not the academy director and had no duty to pay a formal call, refused to go.

sentences.zh: 大考，左遷編修。

translations.literal: At the grand examination he was demoted to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand examination he was demoted to reviser.

sentences.zh: 尋授御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed censor and transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed censor and then promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 昌齊生海邦，習洋盜情狀。

translations.literal: Changqi was born in a coastal region and was familiar with the circumstances of maritime pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi came from the coast and was familiar with the ways of sea pirates.

sentences.zh: 上疏論剿捕事，略曰：「洋匪上岸，率不過一二百人，陸居會匪助兇行劫。

translations.literal: He memorialized the throne on suppression and capture, saying in summary: "When maritime bandits come ashore, they generally number no more than one or two hundred; land-based secret-society bandits assist them in robbery and violence.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on suppression and capture, saying in summary: "When sea bandits come ashore, they usually number no more than one or two hundred men, with local secret-society bandits on land helping them rob and kill.

sentences.zh: 沿海居民皆採捕為生，習拳勇，諳水勢，匪以利誘，往往從匪。

translations.literal: Coastal residents all make their living by fishing and hunting; they are skilled in boxing and martial arts and know the waters well; bandits tempt them with profit, and they often join the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal people live by fishing and hunting; they are trained in boxing and know the waters well, and bandits often lure them with profit into joining the gangs.

sentences.zh: 可以為盜，即可用以捕盜。

translations.literal: Those who can serve as pirates can also be used to capture pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Men who can serve as pirates can also be used to catch them.

sentences.zh: 宜令地方官明示，有能出洋剿捕，或遇匪上岸，殲擒送官驗實者，船物一概充賞。

translations.literal: Local officials should be ordered to make clear that whoever can go to sea to suppress and capture bandits, or when bandits come ashore kills and captures them and delivers them to officials for verification, shall receive the ships and goods entirely as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials should announce clearly that anyone who goes to sea to hunt bandits, or who kills or captures bandits when they come ashore and delivers them to the authorities for verification, shall receive the ships and goods in full as reward.

sentences.zh: 被誘從匪者，能擒盜連船投首，免罪。

translations.literal: Those who were lured into following bandits, if they can capture bandits together with their ships and surrender, shall be exempt from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were lured into following the bandits, if they capture pirates together with their ships and surrender, shall be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 則兵力所未及，丁壯亦必圖賞力捕。

translations.literal: Then where military force cannot reach, able-bodied men will surely strive for reward to capture them by force.
translations.idiomatic: Then even where troops cannot reach, able-bodied men will surely exert themselves for the reward and capture bandits by force.

sentences.zh: 仍令地方各官稽戶口，編保甲，以清其源。

translations.literal: Local officials should still be ordered to check household registers and organize the baojia system, to eliminate the source.
translations.idiomatic: Officials should also be ordered to check household registers and organize the baojia system, so as to cut off the source of the trouble.

sentences.zh: 於各埠訪拏濟匪糧物，各市鎮嚴緝代匪銷贓，俾絕水陸勾通之路。

translations.literal: At each port investigate and arrest those supplying food and goods to bandits; at each market town strictly seize those who dispose of stolen goods for bandits, so as to cut off the routes of communication between water and land.
translations.idiomatic: At every port they should hunt down those who supply bandits with food and goods; at every market town they should strictly arrest those who dispose of stolen goods for the bandits, so as to sever the links between land and sea.

sentences.zh: 庶幾洋面肅清，地方寧謐。

translations.literal: Thus the maritime realm may be cleared and the region made tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the seas may be cleared and the region restored to peace.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年，出為浙江溫處道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiaqing he was sent out as Wen-Chu Circuit intendant of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Jiaqing reign he was appointed Wen-Chu Circuit intendant of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時海寇蔡牽肆擾，昌齊修戰艦，簡軍伍，募人出海繪浙、閩海洋全圖，纖悉備具。

translations.literal: At the time the sea bandit Cai Qian was running rampant; Changqi repaired warships, selected troops, and hired men to go to sea and chart complete maps of the Zhejiang and Fujian seas, with every detail fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the pirate Cai Qian was ravaging the coast; Changqi repaired warships, picked troops, and hired men to go to sea and draw complete charts of the Zhejiang and Fujian waters, down to the smallest detail.

sentences.zh: 每牒報賊情及道里遠近稍有虛妄，必指斥之。

translations.literal: Whenever reports on bandit conditions and distances were slightly false, he invariably called them out.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a dispatch reporting bandit movements or distances was even slightly inaccurate, he rebuked it.

sentences.zh: 與提督李長庚深相結納，俾無掣肘，鞫海盜必詳盡得其情。

translations.literal: He formed a deep alliance with Admiral Li Changgeng so that there would be no hindrance; when interrogating pirates he always thoroughly obtained the full facts.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a close alliance with Admiral Li Changgeng so that neither was hampered by the other, and when questioning pirates he always extracted the full truth.

sentences.zh: 德楞泰奉命按閱閩、浙，議申海禁，謂不數月盜可盡斃。

translations.literal: Delengtai was ordered to inspect Fujian and Zhejiang, proposed imposing a sea ban, and said that within a few months the bandits could all be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Delengtai was ordered to inspect Fujian and Zhejiang, proposed enforcing a sea ban, and said the pirates could all be wiped out within a few months.

sentences.zh: 昌齊曰：「環海居民耕而食者十之五，餘皆捕魚為業。

translations.literal: Changqi said: "Of coastal residents, five-tenths live by farming; the rest all fish for a living.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi said: "Of the people along the coast, half live by farming and the rest live by fishing.

sentences.zh: 若禁其下海，數万漁戶無以為生，激變之咎誰任之？

translations.literal: If they are forbidden to go to sea, tens of thousands of fishing households will have no means to live — who will bear responsibility for the resulting uprising?
translations.idiomatic: If they are forbidden to put to sea, tens of thousands of fishing households will have no way to live — who will answer for the revolt that follows?

sentences.zh: 」德楞泰改容稱善。

translations.literal: " Delengtai changed expression and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: " Delengtai's expression changed and he praised the point.

sentences.zh: 在任五年，以鞫獄遲延，部議鐫級。

translations.literal: After five years in office, because adjudication of cases was delayed, the ministry recommended demotion by one rank.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office he was demoted one rank by the ministry for delays in trying cases.

sentences.zh: 江南、福建大吏闢調，皆不往。

translations.literal: When grand officials of Jiangnan and Fujian opened posts for his transfer, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When senior officials in Jiangnan and Fujian solicited his transfer, he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 歸里，主雷陽粵秀講席。

translations.literal: He returned home and presided over the lecture chair at the Leiyang Yuexiu Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and headed the lecture chair at the Leiyang Yuexiu Academy.

sentences.zh: 修通志。

translations.literal: He compiled the local gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the local gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 考據詳覈，著書終老焉。

translations.literal: His textual research was thorough and precise; he wrote books until his old age.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship was meticulous, and he spent his old age writing books.

sentences.zh: 硃爾賡額，原名友桂，字白泉，漢軍正紅旗人，裔出明代。

translations.literal: Zhu Ergenge, original name Yougui, courtesy name Baiquan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner, descended from the Ming dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ergenge, original name Yougui, courtesy name Baiquan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner and a descendant of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 王父孝純，工詩古文，有異才，由四川知縣歷官至兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiaochun was skilled in poetry and classical prose, possessed extraordinary talent, and rose from county magistrate in Sichuan to Salt Transport Commissioner of Lianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiaochun was accomplished in poetry and classical prose, possessed unusual talent, and rose from county magistrate in Sichuan to Salt Transport Commissioner of Lianghuai.

sentences.zh: 硃爾賡額納貲為兵部主事，充軍機章京，累遷郎中，出為江安糧道。

translations.literal: Zhu Ergenge purchased appointment as a principal secretary in the Ministry of War, served as a Grand Council clerk, was successively promoted to department director, and went out as grain intendant of Jiang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ergenge bought appointment as a principal secretary in the Ministry of War, served as a Grand Council clerk, rose successively to department director, and was then appointed grain intendant of Jiang'an.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督蘇凌阿閽人為和珅舊奴，恣睢用事，廉得其狀，白而逐之。

translations.literal: The Two Jiangs Governor-General Su Ling'a's favorite was an old slave of Heshen who acted tyrannically; Zhu learned of this, reported it, and had him expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Su Ling'a of the Two Jiangs kept a favorite who had been an old slave of Heshen and abused his power; Zhu Ergenge investigated the matter, reported it, and had the man driven out.

sentences.zh: 從總督赴安徽察治劉之協逆黨，株連數百人，多所省釋。

translations.literal: Following the governor-general to Anhui to investigate Liu Zhixie's rebel party, though hundreds were implicated, he released many.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the governor-general to Anhui to investigate Liu Zhixie's rebel associates, although hundreds were implicated, he released many of them.

sentences.zh: 署安徽布政使，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Serving as acting provincial treasurer of Anhui, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as acting provincial treasurer of Anhui, he pleaded illness and retired home.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞改京秩，授戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he petitioned to change to a capital rank; he was appointed Langzhong in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his mother's advanced age, he petitioned for a capital post and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 和珅奴劉全之婿號檳榔蔣者，倚勢奪民產，訟於部，刑責不稍貸。

translations.literal: Betel-nut Jiang, the son-in-law of Liu Quan, Heshen's slave, relied on power to seize people's property; when the case came before the ministry, punishment was not in the least lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Betel-nut Jiang, son-in-law of Liu Quan, a servant of Heshen, had used his connections to seize commoners' property. When the case came before the ministry, Zhu Ergenge showed no leniency in applying the law.

sentences.zh: 西賈利旗產，​​嗾言官疏陳，使得與漢民通售買，下部議，啖以重賄，卻之，持不可。

translations.literal: Western merchants profited from banner estates; they instigated censorial memorials proposing that they be allowed to trade freely with Han commoners. When the matter came to the ministry for deliberation, they tried to tempt him with heavy bribes; he refused and held that it was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Western merchants sought profit from banner lands and induced memorialists to propose opening trade with Han subjects. When the matter came to the ministry, they offered heavy bribes, which he refused, maintaining that the proposal could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 大學士硃珪管部，聞而重之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhu Gui supervised the ministry; hearing of this, he thought highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhu Gui, who oversaw the ministry, heard of this and thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 故事，自告改京官，不外用。

translations.literal: By precedent, those who on their own petition had changed to capital posts were not sent out for external appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent held that officials who had voluntarily transferred to capital posts were not reassigned to provincial service.

sentences.zh: 珪薦其才守可大受，復出為廣東潮州知府。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui recommended his talent and integrity as fit for great responsibility, and he was again sent out as prefect of Chaozhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui recommended him as talented and upright enough for greater responsibility, and he was again posted as prefect of Chaozhou in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 海盜方張，硃濆尤黠悍，乃親歷海壖，治鄉團，調鎮兵千守沿海，斷內奸接濟。

translations.literal: Pirates were flourishing, and Zhu Fen was especially cunning and fierce; he then personally toured the coastal regions, organized village militias, transferred a thousand garrison troops to guard the coast, and cut off supply lines from internal collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: With piracy on the rise and Zhu Fen proving especially cunning and fierce, he personally toured the coast, organized village militias, stationed a thousand garrison troops along the shore, and severed supply lines from collaborators within.

sentences.zh: 濆糧絕，屢敗走台灣，潮盜膽落，因其窮蹙解散之。

translations.literal: When Fen's grain was exhausted, he was repeatedly defeated and fled to Taiwan; the courage of the Chaozhou pirates fell, and taking advantage of their destitution, he dissolved them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Fen's supplies ran out and he was repeatedly defeated and driven to Taiwan, the pirates of Chaozhou lost heart; Zhu Ergenge took advantage of their plight to break up their bands.

sentences.zh: 盜魁黃茂高、許雲湘、王騰魁、楊勝廣、黃德東、關兆奎受撫，選其強幹者編入練勇。

translations.literal: The pirate chiefs Huang Maogao, Xu Yunxiang, Wang Tengkui, Yang Shengguang, Huang Dedong, and Guan Zhaokui accepted pacification; their strongest and most capable followers were selected and organized into trained militia.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate leaders Huang Maogao, Xu Yunxiang, Wang Tengkui, Yang Shengguang, Huang Dedong, and Guan Zhaokui submitted to pacification; their strongest followers were selected and incorporated into militia units.

sentences.zh: 會匪李崇玉踞惠、潮山谷中，時游弋海上，使降人招之自首，硃濆部眾亦有來投者。

translations.literal: The secret-society bandit Li Chongyu held the valleys of Huizhou and Chaozhou and at times cruised at sea; he sent surrendered men to summon him to surrender himself, and some of Zhu Fen's followers also came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The secret-society bandit Li Chongyu held the mountainous borderlands of Huizhou and Chaozhou and sometimes raided at sea. Zhu Ergenge sent former pirates to urge him to surrender, and some of Zhu Fen's followers also came over.

sentences.zh: 會以母憂去，未竟其事，服闋，補雲南曲靖。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, because of his mother's death he left office before the work was finished; after the mourning period ended, he was assigned to Qujing in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He then left office to observe mourning for his mother before the work was finished; when the mourning period ended, he was assigned to Qujing in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十四年，百齡為兩廣總督，疏請調硃爾賡額廣東，擢高廉道，署督糧道，剿匪事一以倚之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing, Bailing became Governor-General of Liangguang and memorialized requesting the transfer of Zhu Ergenge to Guangdong; he was promoted to intendant of the Gaolian Circuit, acted as grain transport commissioner, and on bandit-suppression matters Bailing relied entirely on him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 14 (1809), Bailing became Governor-General of the Two Guangs and memorialized to have Zhu Ergenge transferred to Guangdong, promoting him to intendant of the Gaolian Circuit and acting grain commissioner, relying on him entirely for anti-piracy operations.

sentences.zh: 勘海口砲台舊在山上，發砲輒從桅頂過，悉改建於山麓，屢碎盜艦，挫其鋒。

translations.literal: On inspecting the Haikou batteries, he found they had formerly been on the mountain and that cannon fire always passed over the mast tops; he had them all rebuilt at the foot of the mountain, repeatedly smashing pirate ships and blunting their offensive.
translations.idiomatic: He found that the Haikou batteries, built on the heights, sent shots sailing over enemy masts; he had them all relocated to the foothills, repeatedly smashing pirate vessels and blunting their offensive.

sentences.zh: 暫改運鹽由陸，撤紅單船入內港，以杜接濟。

translations.literal: Salt transport was temporarily changed to go by land, and red-stamped ships were withdrawn from inner harbors, to block supply lines.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was temporarily moved overland, and licensed red-stamp shipping vessels were barred from inner harbors to cut off supplies to the pirates.

sentences.zh: 戒並海郡縣嚴斷水米，如在潮州時。

translations.literal: He ordered the coastal prefectures and counties to strictly cut off water and grain, as he had done in Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered coastal prefectures and counties to enforce the same strict embargo on food and freshwater that he had used in Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 匪勢漸蹙，用舊降人招郭學顯就撫。

translations.literal: As the bandits' power was gradually pressed, he used former surrendered men to summon Guo Xuexian to accept pacification.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels grew increasingly cornered, he employed former pirates to persuade Guo Xuexian to surrender.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鄭一妻與張保仔率眾逾萬泊虎門，要總督親至海口面議，文武噤莫敢決，硃爾賡額獨進曰：「保仔自知罪大，眾多無糧，拂其請，將死鬥。

translations.literal: Before long, Zheng Yi's wife and Zhang Baozai led more than ten thousand men and anchored at Humen, demanding that the governor-general come in person to Haikou for face-to-face talks. The civil and military officials were silent and dared not decide; Zhu Ergenge alone stepped forward and said: "Baozai knows his crimes are great and his followers lack grain; if we reject their request, they will fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zheng Yi's widow and Zhang Baozai anchored more than ten thousand men at Humen and demanded that the governor-general come to Haikou in person. The civil and military officers were too frightened to decide. Zhu Ergenge alone stepped forward: "Baozai knows his crimes are grave and his men are starving. If we refuse, they will fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 請撤兵衛，單舟迳詣，諭以恩威，必可集事。

translations.literal: Please withdraw the military escort and go directly in a single boat to instruct them with both grace and authority; the matter can surely be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw the escort and go alone in a single boat to appeal to both mercy and force — that will surely settle it.

sentences.zh: 」先遣南海、番禺兩令往傳命，使熟籌而志堅。

translations.literal: " He first sent the magistrates of Nanhai and Panyu to convey the orders, so that they might deliberate thoroughly and resolve firmly.
translations.idiomatic: " He first sent the magistrates of Nanhai and Panyu to deliver the message so they could prepare carefully and steel their resolve.

sentences.zh: 翌晨，從百齡登舟，行四十里，見列艦數百，夾水如衢，舉砲迎，聲震城中。

translations.literal: The next morning, following Bailing, he boarded a boat and traveled forty li; he saw hundreds of ships lined up on both sides of the water like a street, raising cannon in salute with a sound that shook the city.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he accompanied Bailing aboard ship. After forty li they saw hundreds of vessels massed on both sides of the channel like a street; the pirates fired salutes that shook the city.

sentences.zh: 請總督過舟，叱之曰：「保仔當泥首乞命，如仍驕肆遲疑，無死所矣！

translations.literal: He asked the governor-general to cross to their boat and rebuked them, saying: "Baozai ought to come with dust on his head begging for his life; if he still acts arrogantly and hesitates, he will have nowhere to die!
translations.idiomatic: Bailing was invited aboard the pirates' ship, where Zhu Ergenge rebuked Zhang Baozai: "You should come begging for your life with dust on your head. If you remain arrogant and hesitate, you will have nowhere to die!"

sentences.zh: 」迨晡，保仔登舟，請留三千人招西路賊烏石二，不聽則擒之以自贖，許之，給米千石慰遣。

translations.literal: " By dusk, Baozai boarded the boat and asked to retain three thousand men to recruit the western-route bandit Wushi Er; if refused, he would capture him to redeem himself. This was granted, and a thousand shi of rice was given to comfort and send them off.
translations.idiomatic: " By evening Zhang Baozai came aboard and asked to keep three thousand men to recruit the western pirate Wushi Er, offering to capture him if refused as proof of loyalty. This was granted, and a thousand shi of rice was given to provision and send them off.

sentences.zh: 保仔乃使餘眾登岸受撫，自起椗出洋。

translations.literal: Baozai then had the remaining multitude go ashore to accept pacification, while he himself raised anchor and put out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baozai then sent the rest of his followers ashore to surrender while he himself weighed anchor and put to sea.

sentences.zh: 群謂其所散皆罷弱，自留精銳，得米將不可製，笑應之曰：「此不必以口舌爭。

translations.literal: The group said that those he sent away were all weak, while he kept the elite; once he got the rice he would become uncontrollable. Smiling, he replied: "This is not worth arguing about with words.
translations.idiomatic: Others said he had sent ashore only the weak while keeping his best men, and that the rice would make him impossible to control. Zhu Ergenge smiled and replied: "That is not worth arguing about.

sentences.zh: 」至期，保仔果誘烏石二至高州，誅之。

translations.literal: " When the deadline came, Baozai indeed lured Wushi Er to Gaozhou and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: " When the time came, Zhang Baozai indeed lured Wushi Er to Gaozhou and killed him.

sentences.zh: 海盜悉平，以功獲優敘，賜花翎。

translations.literal: The sea pirates were all pacified; for his merit he received a favorable promotion record and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: With the pirates fully suppressed, he received distinguished commendation for his service and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋調署南韶道。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to serve as acting intendant of the Nanshao Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to serve as acting intendant of the Nanshao Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十六年，河決李家樓，特命百齡為兩江總督治河事，調硃爾賡額為江南鹽巡道。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Yellow River burst at Lijialou; Bailing was specially ordered to be Governor-General of Liangjiang to manage river affairs, and Zhu Ergenge was transferred to be salt patrol commissioner for Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 16 (1811), the Yellow River broke at Lijialou. Bailing was specially appointed Governor-General of the Two Jiangs to handle river works, and Zhu Ergenge was transferred to salt patrol commissioner for Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 至則佐百齡定計，接築洪澤湖口束清壩，逼溜刷深太平河，使水有所歸。

translations.literal: On arrival he assisted Bailing in devising a plan, linking construction of the Shuqing Dam at the Hongze Lake outlet to force the current to scour the Taiping River deeper so the water would have somewhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he helped Bailing plan construction, linking the Shuqing Dam at the Hongze Lake outlet to force the current to scour the Taiping River deeper so the water would have an outlet.

sentences.zh: 次年，李家樓決口合龍，新築格堤遏水與大堤平。

translations.literal: The next year the Lijialou breach was closed, and the newly built containment dike held the water level even with the main embankment.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Lijialou breach was closed, and the newly built containment dike held the water level even with the main embankment.

sentences.zh: 初，當事主守格堤​​，奉嚴旨，失守者從軍法。

translations.literal: At first those in charge were ordered mainly to defend the containment dike; under a stern imperial command, anyone who lost it would face military punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At first officials were ordered under strict imperial command to hold the containment dike; anyone who lost it would face military punishment.

sentences.zh: 至是見事危急，請改守大堤，聽河溜穿格堤而下，免旁洩之險。

translations.literal: Seeing the situation turn critical, he requested to shift defense to the main dike and allow the river current to pass through the containment dike, avoiding the danger of a side breach.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the situation turn critical, he petitioned to shift defense to the main dike and allow the current to pass through the containment dike, avoiding the risk of a side breach.

sentences.zh: 又新築減壩受水攻，展側上游築斜壩挑水，數日壩根掛淤乃穩固。

translations.literal: He also built new spillway dams to receive the water's attack, extending upstream with slanted dikes to divert the flow; after several days silt accumulated at the dam base and the works became stable.
translations.idiomatic: He also built new spillway dams to take the brunt of the water, extending upstream with slanted dikes to redirect the flow; after several days silt accumulated at the base and the works held firm.

sentences.zh: 所籌措工事悉合機宜。

translations.literal: All the works he planned and arranged were entirely suited to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Every engineering measure he planned proved well suited to conditions.

sentences.zh: 葦蕩營久為弊藪，樵兵空額無人，營員領帑，臨時僱募，弁目專其利。

translations.literal: The reed marsh camps had long been a nest of abuses: authorized cutter posts sat empty with no men, camp officers received funds and temporarily hired labor, and sergeants monopolized the profit.
translations.idiomatic: The reed marsh camps had long been riddled with corruption: authorized cutter posts sat empty while camp officers collected salaries, hired men on the spot, and noncommissioned officers kept the profits.

sentences.zh: 又為灘棍所持，盪料歸灘棍者十五六。

translations.literal: They were also controlled by beach bullies; fifteen or sixteen parts out of ten of the marsh reeds went to the beach bullies.
translations.idiomatic: Beach thugs also controlled the trade, taking fifteen or sixteen tenths of the marsh reed harvest.

sentences.zh: 歸弁目者十二三，歸工用者十一二，歲僅得葦十數万束。

translations.literal: Twelve or thirteen parts went to the sergeants, eleven or twelve to actual labor, and each year only a hundred thousand-odd bundles of reeds were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Sergeants took twelve or thirteen tenths, actual labor got eleven or twelve, and only a hundred thousand-odd bundles of reeds were harvested each year.

sentences.zh: 百齡檄硃爾賡額督治其事，乃請以盪地不產柴者給樵兵，人四十畝，給牛具籽種，建棚廠以居，盪始有兵。

translations.literal: Bailing ordered Zhu Ergenge to supervise reform of the matter; he then requested that marsh land that produced no firewood be given to the reed-cutters, forty mu per man, with oxen, tools, and seed supplied, and sheds and workshops built for them to live in, so that the marshes finally had actual personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Bailing ordered Zhu Ergenge to reform the system. He proposed granting non-productive marshland to cutters — forty mu each — with oxen, tools, and seed, and building barracks so the marshes finally had actual personnel.

sentences.zh: 濬溝渠便筏出入，採運始及遠，建衙署俾營員常年駐盪，民挾制偷竊者有禁，盪始有官。

translations.literal: He dredged canals to facilitate raft traffic, so harvesting and transport could reach distant areas; he built yamen offices so camp officers could be stationed in the marshes year-round, and prohibited common people from exploiting the situation to steal — so the marshes finally had official governance.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged channels for raft traffic so harvesting could reach distant areas, built offices for year-round official presence, and curbed theft by locals — so the marshes finally had proper governance.

sentences.zh: 受事之年，採足正額二百四十萬束。

translations.literal: In the year he took office, the full quota of 2.4 million bundles was harvested.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year in charge, the full quota of 2.4 million bundles was harvested.

sentences.zh: 於是灘棍之利盡失，廳員得料抵價，少所沾潤，皆不便之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the beach bullies lost their profits entirely; the hall officers, who received materials at assessed prices, had little grease left and all found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The beach thugs lost their profits; yamen staff who had skimmed from material payments found their perquisites cut — and all resented the change.

sentences.zh: 適有船兵中途改束，斤重不敷，八廳藉欲撼搖全局。

translations.literal: Just then boat soldiers midway changed the bundle standard and the weight fell short; the eight hall offices seized the opportunity and sought to shake the whole system.
translations.idiomatic: Just then transport crews altered bundle sizes en route so weights fell short; officials from eight sub-offices seized the chance to try to overturn the whole reform.

sentences.zh: 百齡悉其奸，偕河督察訊，硃爾賡額往勘定十七年新葦，每束箍口以二尺八寸為率，增舊三寸，估右營得葦八百萬束；

translations.literal: Bailing knew their trickery and, together with the river inspection censor, conducted an inquiry; Zhu Ergenge went to survey and fix standards for the new reeds of the seventeenth year, taking two chi eight cun as the standard for each bundle mouth, three cun larger than before, and estimated that the right camp would yield eight million bundles.
translations.idiomatic: Bailing saw through the scheme and joined the river inspector in an inquiry. Zhu Ergenge went to set standards for the new reed harvest of year 17: bundle mouths at two chi eight cun, three cun larger than before; the right camp was estimated at eight million bundles.

sentences.zh: 會署江寧布政使，未及估左營。

translations.literal: He was concurrently acting Jiangning financial commissioner and had not yet reached estimating the left camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently acting Jiangning financial commissioner and had not yet assessed the left camp.

sentences.zh: 時河督陳鳳翔為百齡所劾，自訴於朝，命尚書松筠、侍郎初彭齡按訊，牽及葦蕩事。

translations.literal: At the time River Governor Chen Fengxiang had been impeached by Bailing and appealed to the throne; Songyun and Vice Minister Chu Pengling were ordered to investigate, and the reed marsh affair was drawn into the case.
translations.idiomatic: River governor Chen Fengxiang, whom Bailing had impeached, appealed to the throne. Songyun and Vice Minister Chu Pengling were sent to investigate, and the reed marsh affair was drawn into the case.

sentences.zh: 廳員熒說，嗾驗尾幫，舟載餘葦九百束，據其重率，以衡已收三百萬束之數，斥為不足，遂被劾虛糜錢糧，苦累樵兵，遣戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Hall officers whispered persuasion and instigated an inspection of the trailing convoy: a boat carrying nine hundred remaining bundles of reeds; based on their weight rate, they measured against the three million bundles already collected, denounced the amount as insufficient, and he was then impeached for wastefully spending funds and grain and oppressing the reed-cutters, and sent into exile at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen staff spread rumors and instigated an inspection of the trailing convoy: a boat with nine hundred leftover bundles was weighed, and by that standard the three million bundles already collected were declared short. Zhu Ergenge was impeached for wasting public funds and burdening the cutters, and exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 時冤之。

translations.literal: At the time many considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Many at the time considered this a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 硃爾賡額因百齡前劾鳳翔詞不盡實，獄無結正，原以身任，遂不辯。

translations.literal: Zhu Ergenge felt that Bailing's earlier impeachment of Fengxiang had not been fully truthful and the case had no conclusive resolution; he had originally intended to bear responsibility himself, and therefore did not defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ergenge felt that Bailing's earlier impeachment of Chen Fengxiang had not been fully truthful and the case remained unsettled; he had intended to accept responsibility himself and therefore did not defend himself.

sentences.zh: 在戍六年，放還，久之，卒。

translations.literal: He spent six years in exile, was released and returned, and after a long time died.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in exile he was released; he died some time later.

sentences.zh: 查崇華，字九峰，安徽涇縣人。

translations.literal: Cha Chonghua, courtesy name Jiufeng, was a native of Jing County, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cha Chonghua, styled Jiufeng, was a native of Jing County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少孤，遊福建傭書。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he wandered to Fujian copying books for hire.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned as a boy, he went to Fujian and made a living copying books.

sentences.zh: 久之，福州將軍魁倫闢佐幕，甚見信任。

translations.literal: After a long time, Fujian Regional Commander Kuilun invited him to his staff and greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: In time Fujian Regional Commander Kuilun took him onto his staff, where he won deep trust.

sentences.zh: 魁倫劾總督伍拉納、巡撫浦霖，即命署總督，治其獄。

translations.literal: When Kuilun impeached Governor-General Wulana and Governor Pulín, he was immediately ordered to act as governor-general and try their cases.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuilun impeached Governor-General Wulana and Governor Pulín, he was at once appointed acting governor-general to try their cases.

sentences.zh: 閩地瘠苦，歷任大吏責供張無藝，所屬羅織大戶勒賄，民不堪命，至是貪酷之吏悉伏辜。

translations.literal: Fujian's land was poor and bitter; successive high officials demanded lavish hospitality without limit, and subordinates fabricated charges against wealthy households to extort bribes; the people could not bear it — at this time all the greedy and cruel officials were brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was poor and hard-pressed; successive governors had demanded lavish hospitality without limit, while subordinates framed wealthy families to extort bribes until the people could endure no more. Under Chonghua's prosecution, the most grasping officials were all punished.

sentences.zh: 崇華名聞於時。

translations.literal: Chonghua's name became known in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua's reputation spread at the time.

sentences.zh: 納貲為通判，留福建。

translations.literal: He purchased appointment as subprefect and remained in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He bought appointment as subprefect and stayed on in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十四年，海盜蔡牽平，以功賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing, when the sea pirate Cai Qian was pacified, he was awarded the peacock feather for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 14, when the pirate Cai Qian was suppressed, he received the peacock feather for his service.

sentences.zh: 硃渥欲歸誠，未決，崇華隻身至海舶，諭以禍福，遂受降。

translations.literal: Zhu Wo wished to surrender but had not decided; Chonghua went alone to the sea vessel, instructed him on fortune and disaster, and he then accepted surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wo wished to surrender but hesitated; Chonghua went alone to his ship, explained the consequences, and won his submission.

sentences.zh: 十七年，署台灣淡水同知。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he served as acting subprefect of Tamsui, Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he served as acting subprefect of Tamsui in Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 高媽達妖言惑眾，捕獲，訊得劉林、祝現謀以次年閏八月望在京師舉事，四方起應之。

translations.literal: Gao Mada used demonic words to delude the masses; when captured and interrogated, it was learned that Liu Lin and Zhu Xian plotted to rise in the capital on the full moon of the intercalary eighth month of the following year, with responses rising in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mada used sorcery to mislead the people. When captured and questioned, he revealed that Liu Lin and Zhu Xian planned an uprising in the capital on the full moon of the intercalary eighth month of the following year, with coordinated risings across the realm.

sentences.zh: 崇華牒請奏聞，大吏以其語不經，置之，僅以傳教罪誅高媽達。

translations.literal: Chonghua memorialized requesting that the throne be informed; the high officials, holding his words incredible, set the matter aside and only executed Gao Mada on the charge of preaching heterodox doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua memorialized urging that the court be informed, but senior officials dismissed his report as incredible and executed Gao Mada only for illegal preaching.

sentences.zh: 至十八年九月十五日，果有林清、祝現之變，劉林者即林清別名也。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the eighteenth year, the affair of Lin Qing and Zhu Xian indeed occurred; Liu Lin was none other than Lin Qing's alias.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the eighteenth year, the uprising of Lin Qing and Zhu Xian broke out exactly as foretold; Liu Lin was in fact Lin Qing's alias.

sentences.zh: 自高媽達伏法，福建匪黨巳解散，得無事。

translations.literal: After Gao Mada was executed by law, the bandit gangs of Fujian had already dispersed, and the province remained untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Mada was executed, Fujian's rebel bands had already broken up, and the province remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 尋以道員謁選，授河南南汝光道。

translations.literal: Soon, as a circuit intendant awaiting selection, he was appointed to the Nanyu-Guang Circuit in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as a circuit intendant awaiting assignment, he was appointed to the Nanyu-Guang Circuit in Henan.

sentences.zh: 教匪鉅魁劉松久在逃，懸緝十餘載，偵知潛匿安徽宿州傳教，捕獲之。

translations.literal: The great rebel chief Liu Song had long been at large; wanted for more than ten years, it was learned he was secretly hiding in Suzhou, Anhui, preaching his doctrine, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Liu Song had been at large for more than a decade. Intelligence placed him secretly preaching in Suzhou, Anhui, and Chonghua captured him.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，補陝西鳳邠道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, he was assigned to the Feng-Bin Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he was appointed to the Feng-Bin Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 值大軍徵張格爾，調駐嘉峪關治軍需。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Zhang Ge'er, he was transferred to station at Jiayuguan to manage military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force marched against Zhang Ge'er, he was posted at Jiayuguan to manage military supplies.

sentences.zh: 自川、楚軍興，將吏習於糜費，崇華一主覈實，以內地馬駝出關不耐寒苦，關外有台站應付，長僱徒糜芻秣，悉罷之，節帑甚鉅。

translations.literal: Since the armies of Sichuan and Hubei had risen, officers and officials were accustomed to waste; Chonghua insisted on verification throughout. Because horses and camels from the interior could not endure the cold beyond the pass, and relay stations beyond the pass should provide transport, he abolished long-term hiring of laborers and wasteful fodder, saving very large sums from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Sichuan-Hubei campaigns, officers had grown used to extravagance; Chonghua insisted on strict accounting. Horses and camels from the interior could not endure the cold beyond the pass, where relay stations should provide transport, so he abolished long-term hiring and wasteful fodder contracts, saving enormous sums from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 凡三署按察使，治獄明慎。

translations.literal: He thrice served as acting surveillance commissioner and tried cases with clarity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: He served three times as acting surveillance commissioner and handled cases with clarity and care.

sentences.zh: 以老乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: Citing old age, he petitioned to return home and died.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded old age, retired home, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：剿平教匪，不獨賴將帥戮力，一時守土之吏，與有勞焉。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Suppressing and pacifying the sect rebels did not rely solely on generals exerting themselves in slaughter; the local officials of the time also shared in the labor.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes: Suppressing the White Lotus rebels did not depend on generals alone; local officials of the day also bore their share of the burden.

sentences.zh: 最顯者為四川劉清，而方積亦倡行堅壁清野，保障一方，後復屢定番亂，蜀人與清並稱。

translations.literal: The most prominent was Liu Qing of Sichuan, while Fang Ji also pioneered the fortify-and-clear policy, securing one region; afterward he repeatedly pacified tribal rebellions, and the people of Shu ranked him with Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The most celebrated was Liu Qing of Sichuan, but Fang Ji also pioneered the scorched-earth and fortified-defense strategy that secured Liangshan, and later repeatedly pacified tribal uprisings; Sichuan people ranked him alongside Liu Qing.

sentences.zh: 他如硃爾漢之保鞏昌，楊頀之清叛產、撫難民，廖寅之擒劉之協，皆卓有建樹。

translations.literal: Others such as Zhu Erhan's defense of Gongchang, Yang Hu's clearing of rebel property and relief of refugees, and Liao Yin's capture of Liu Zhixie all made outstanding achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Others too made outstanding marks: Zhu Erhan's defense of Gongchang, Yang Hu's clearing of rebel estates and relief of war victims, and Liao Yin's capture of Liu Zhixie.

sentences.zh: 陳昌齊、硃爾賡額於治海寇並具謀略，而硃爾賡額功尤顯矣。

translations.literal: Chen Changqi and Zhu Ergenge both possessed strategy in dealing with sea bandits, while Zhu Ergenge's achievements were especially conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Changqi and Zhu Ergenge both showed strategic talent against sea pirates, though Zhu Ergenge's achievements were especially striking.

sentences.zh: 查崇華預發林清逆謀，為疆臣所格；

translations.literal: Cha Chonghua forewarned of Lin Qing's rebel plot but was blocked by frontier governors;
translations.idiomatic: Cha Chonghua had forewarned of Lin Qing's conspiracy but was overruled by provincial governors;

sentences.zh: 及筦西征軍需，以撙節稱，故同著於篇。

translations.literal: when he later managed western campaign military supplies, he was praised for economy, and therefore is recorded together in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: when he later managed supplies for the western campaigns, he was praised for thrift, and is therefore included in this chapter.
